title: Dependency Injection and Configuration in Azure Functions
description: Apply dependency injection and manage configuration settings in Azure Functions using the isolated worker model.

data.text: Dependency injection (DI) lets you register and inject services into your functions, just like in ASP.NET Core. This makes your code testable, modular, and easier to maintain.
In the isolated worker model, you use the standard .NET `IHostBuilder` to configure DI in Program.cs.

data.title: Program.cs — Dependency Injection Setup

data.text: Configuration values are stored in Application Settings. In local development, they live in `local.settings.json`. In Azure, they live in the Function App's Configuration blade.

data.title: C# — Reading Configuration in a Function
Never Hardcode Secrets
data.text: Always use Application Settings for connection strings, API keys, and secrets. The `local.settings.json` file should never be committed to source control. In Azure, configure secrets through Key Vault references for production.

terms.definition: A design pattern where services are provided to a class rather than created inside it.
The .NET interface for reading configuration values from app settings.
Key-value pairs stored in the Function App configuration (local.settings.json locally, Azure portal in the cloud).

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: DI works the same way as in ASP.NET Core
Configuration lives in app settings, not in code
Inject IConfiguration to read settings in functions
data.takeaway: Use DI and configuration properly to make your functions testable and maintainable.
